title: Kenyan Garlic Bread
community: Urban Kenya — the universal restaurant accompaniment
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Garlic Bread — a whole baguette or ciabatta slathered with garlic-herb butter, wrapped in foil, and baked until the butter has melted throughout, then opened and toasted until golden. The side dish that everyone reaches for first — and always runs out before the meal ends.
longDesc: Garlic bread appears on every Nairobi restaurant table alongside pasta, soups, salads, and grills. Done properly — with good bread, real butter, generous garlic, and fresh herbs — it is one of the most satisfying accompaniments in the restaurant repertoire.
steps: Beat softened butter with garlic, herbs, salt, and pepper until combined.
Slice bread at an angle at 2cm intervals, cutting ¾ of the way through — do not cut all the way through.
Spread garlic butter generously into each cut and over the top.
Open foil. Bake 3—5 more minutes until golden and lightly toasted.
chefTips: Room temperature butter blends with garlic more smoothly than cold.
Be generous with the butter — restaurant garlic bread is always more buttery than home versions.
The final toasting outside the foil is what creates the crispy top.
commonMistakes: Cold butter — does not blend with garlic.
Not opening the foil for the final toast.
cookingScience: The foil creates a steam environment that allows the butter to melt throughout the bread and penetrate the crumb. Opening the foil for the final toasting exposes the buttered surface to direct dry heat, creating Maillard browning on the surface while the interior remains soft and buttery.
sustainabilityTips: Make garlic butter in batches and freeze — always ready for a restaurant-quality side in minutes.
servedWith: Every pasta, soup, and salad in this category
storage: Assembled unbaked garlic bread freezes for 2 months.
reheating: Bake directly from frozen — add 5 minutes to time.
culturalNote: Garlic bread is one of those dishes that transcends its simplicity — at every level of Nairobi's restaurant scene, from the most casual café to the finest hotel, garlic bread arrives and is gone before the main course.
